LLM_description:
Situation:
Joint Task Force logistics are operating in a contested sector with multiple forward units dispersed across valleys, urban belts, and ridge lines. Ground resupply is the primary mode due to limited air availability and persistent enemy threats (IEDs, indirect fire, ambush). Key depots—Supply Depot Bravo, Logistics Hub Delta, and Ammunition Depot Echo—must sustain forward elements including Infantry Battalion Viper at FOB Alpha, Armored Cavalry Squadron Talon at COP Hammer, and additional maneuver, fires, engineer, medical, and aviation support units. Roads vary in stability; certain corridors require route clearance, electronic countermeasures, and overwatch. Weather and choke points may constrain convoy timing. Depot stock levels fluctuate by supply type and day, and demand at forward units is time-sensitive.

Mission:
Deliver required supplies to all forward units throughout the operational period while minimizing total cost, including transport, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment, and fixed route security risk costs.

Execution/Concept:
- Depots will push shipments by supply type to forward units each day. Outbound flows from any depot are limited by available stocks per supply type and day. Movements will be prioritized to meet critical demands; unmet demand is permitted only as slack, incurring shortage penalties.
- Convoys will be sized to vehicle capacity by accounting for the volume of each supply type loaded. Vehicles assigned to any depot–unit corridor must travel only on routes designated as active.
- Route activation is a deliberate decision. Activating a route (sending any vehicles on that corridor for the day) triggers a fixed Risk Cost representing the security overhead—escort teams, EOD/route clearance, overwatch, and coordination—regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched on that route. This cost is separate from transport costs and applies per route-day activated.
- Fleet availability is constrained. Total vehicles dispatched across all routes each day cannot exceed the available fleet. Movements will be consolidated to reduce the number of activated routes and associated risk overhead, while balancing transport costs and the penalty for unmet demand.
- Transport costs vary by corridor and day due to distance, terrain, and threat posture. Risk-costed routes through exposed valleys and dense urban areas will be used only when necessary. Engineering and security assets will be synchronized to support activated routes; nonessential movements will be deferred or rerouted to safer corridors where feasible.
- The distribution plan will optimize flows from depots to units to meet demands at minimum total operational cost, subject to depot capacity, convoy capacity, route activation, and fleet size constraints.
